item.title: KubeCon NA 2026 Live: The Identity Crisis of AI Agents and the First Announcements from Salt Lake City
item.description: The identity crisis of agents, the integration of MCP into platforms like OpenShift, and the packaged management of agent skills are not fringe topics but the central construction sites for 2027. The coming months will show whether the outlined solution approaches — per-instance identities, versioned skills, and platform-agnostic AI gateways — prove themselves in practice.

item.title: Security Risks of Deploying Vibe-Coded Apps to Production, and Who Fixes Each One
item.description: The main security concerns with deploying vibe-coded apps to production are code-level flaws the builder never reviewed (injection, broken authorization, insecure defaults), risky dependencies, hardcoded secrets, over-permissive infrastructure, and no record of who changed what.

item.title: GitHub availability report: October 2026
item.description: The short version of October: we added substantial independently scalable Azure capacity and removed several ways that failures could escalate. Actions jobs stayed queued or failed to start because the service that assigns jobs to GitHub-hosted runners stopped working reliably. We traced the failures to the networking issue.

item.title: Two small models ship in my Markdown editor. Three more didn't.
item.description: Each model picks one answer from a fixed list, like which language a code block is in. It got 391 suggestions right at 93.8% precision, against 380 at 93.1% for the model already in the app. Marksage is a Markdown editor I built.

item.title: The Kubernetes Upgrade Trap: A Practical Roadmap to Escape Deprecated APIs, Broken Add-ons, and Endless Delays
item.description: Applications, Helm charts, operators, admission controllers, networking components, storage drivers, monitoring agents, and automation tools must all support the target version. Let's build a practical roadmap that helps teams stop postponing Kubernetes upgrades and start treating them as regular platform maintenance. For example, a workload might still use an API that Kubernetes deprecated several releases ago.

item.title: Rider 2026.3 for Game Development: Lua and Verse Plugins, Better C++ Debugging, and Closer Godot Integration
item.description: This release connects Rider more closely with the Godot Editor, improves debugging for Unreal Engine and custom C++ engines, adds support for Unity CoreCLR Players, and introduces new Lua and Verse plugins in Beta. For a lighter, Verse-focused setup, open the generated .code-workspace file.

item.title: Node.js Document Upload and Signed Download from Private Object Storage for Logistics
item.description: An object key can make operational boundaries obvious: The snapshot ID matters more than the filename. A logistics customer can upload several documents named delivery-note.pdf , and a replacement should not silently change the bytes that an earlier audit refers to. It keeps the authorization decision testable and prevents a storage SDK from becoming the place where tenant policy is hidden.

item.title: Front End Observability: Why Your window.onerror Reports Say "Script error." (and How to Fix Them)
item.description: A practical guide to browser error monitoring with window.onerror, covering the cross-origin blind spot, resource failures that never bubble, and error reports that die when the tab closes. MDN also notes that it only fires for script errors thrown synchronously, such as during initial load or inside event handlers. Assigning window.onerror replaces whatever was there.

item.title: The Hard Part of AI Music Isn't Generation—It's Everything Around It
item.description: It is building a music workflow that behaves like the rest of your production system. What does it cost to keep this feature available through both busy and idle periods, including failed attempts, retries, storage, and engineering time? Treat generation as a job, not an HTTP response Audio generation is long-running work.

item.title: What’s fixed in IntelliJ IDEA 2026.3
item.description: IntelliJ IDEA 2026.3 ships over 1,000 bug fixes and over 300 performance fixes . Among others, Spring Boot inlay hints , property highlighting , and JPA entity analysis no longer stall the editor. We removed excessive index updates when a second project closes during indexing and made the workspace model copy files lazily .

item.title: Solving Flaky Playwright Tests: How We Automated E2E Generation with an AI Agent and MCP
item.description: Maintaining E2E test suites is one of those engineering tasks we know is critical, but teams often push aside because scaffolding and debugging selectors feels like an endless chore. In this post, I want to break down an architectural approach to solving this: using an autonomous AI agent that explores web apps, infers user journeys, and generates standard Playwright code with MCP support.

item.title: Predicting and detecting failures: How Azure strengthens reliability for mission-critical workloads
item.description: Takeaway : Azure Failure Prediction and Detection (AFPD) is Microsoft Azure’s end-to-end system aiming to catch hardware failures before they interrupt a workload, not after. SAP workloads offer a compelling example of AFPD’s value, illustrating why preventing interruptions matters for mission-critical services.

item.title: The eMudhra Certificate Authority Compromise: What It Means for TeamCity
item.description: Starting with versions 2026.2.2 and 2026.1.6 , TeamCity shows a health report if the installation still trusts affected certificates, along with remediation steps. item.title: Final Fantasy 14: Evercold's story will have a faster tempo, with worldbuilding in side quests, says Yoshi-P—but I'm not sure that was the problem with Dawntrail

However, I don't think the issue in Dawntrail was its over-emphasis on worldbuilding, it was a lack of interest in how that worldbuilding connected to character.

item.title: Empowering AI Agents with agent-desktop
item.description: The agent-desktop repository addresses the challenge of enabling AI agents to effectively interact with desktop applications across different operating systems. By leveraging the OS accessibility tree, it allows agents to read and operate applications without pixel matching, which is often unreliable.

item.title: How do AI agents authenticate? (The problem nobody has solved yet)
item.description: There's no reason agent authentication shouldn't. For agents that need a stable identity across runs, generate once and store the private key. When it calls a tool, the server logs exactly which DID called — not "some agent using the shared service token.

item.title: Your coding agent's sandbox is off. Here's how to turn it on without breaking everything.
item.description: After an hour you either turn the sandbox off or add broad rules ("allow all of ~") that quietly undo it. The agent wrote files that a trusted tool outside the sandbox later acted on: hook configs, IDE task files, git metadata. That is the important lesson for anyone configuring a sandbox: the dangerous permission isn't "write anywhere", it's "write to a file something else will execute later".

item.title: The Local Loop Is the Architecture
item.description: An agent is not a service with a prompt bolted on. That boundary will not appear in production. The thing they can share is a protocol at the edge of the privileged resource, and a loop that runs all three processes where a human can still watch a retry happen.

item.title: RepoSage: Local-First GitHub Audits with Open-Weight Gemma 4 & Anti-Hallucination Gates
